Executive Summary

A personal Friday assistant for one PM that reads the week's own meetings and email, drafts a follow-up per customer conversation plus a weekly status note, and saves them to OneDrive for review. Recommended route: Cowork plugins, Medium complexity, Stage 1 only.

The dominant work type is Delegated personal work: the PM who asks is the PM who consumes the result (SEC-01, UX-01), reading only their own data (DATA-01, DATA-02). Selection, collection and saving are deterministic and do not need an LLM; only drafting (FR-03, FR-04) uses AI. All in-scope IDs are met in Stage 1, so no Foundry or pro-code escalation is justified.

First-Draft Recommendation

Primary route: Cowork plugins (31/35). Dominant work type is Delegated personal work for one user (SEC-01, UX-01); Stage 1 meets all in-scope IDs; no route has a failed gate; Cowork scores 31/35.

Hybrid composition: Cowork skill for drafting (FR-03, FR-04) + plugins/tools for own mail, calendar and OneDrive (DATA-01, DATA-02, FR-05) + deterministic customer-domain rule (FR-02); no Copilot Studio, Foundry or pro-code component.

Fallback: DA + skills (27/35) run manually each Friday if a scheduled personal routine is not available. Standard harness is not recommended: the work is one person's delegated drafting, not a shared predictable conversation.

Questions to Confirm

  • How should a 'customer conversation' be identified — external email domains, a list of accounts, or meeting tags?
  • Can the assistant read Teams meeting transcripts, or only calendar invites and email threads?
  • Which OneDrive folder and format do you want (one file per follow-up, or one weekly document)?

Business Problem and Opportunity

Each Friday the PM must recall every customer conversation of the week, write follow-ups and compile a status note by hand. Items get missed and the routine consumes time. Opportunity: draft everything automatically from the PM's own week, keeping the PM in control of what is sent (GR-01).

  • Fewer missed customer follow-ups (FR-02, FR-03)
  • Status note ready for review each Friday (FR-04)
  • Zero unreviewed outbound messages (GR-01)

In-Scope and Out-of-Scope Capabilities

In scope

  • FR-01 — Run automatically every Friday for the past week (Mon–Fri).
  • DATA-01 — Read the user's own meetings from the week (calendar events; transcripts/notes only if available).
  • DATA-02 — Read the user's own emails from the week.
  • FR-02 — Identify each customer conversation in the week's meetings and emails.
  • FR-03 — Draft one follow-up email per customer conversation.
  • FR-04 — Draft one weekly status note summarising the week.
  • FR-05 — Save all drafts in the user's OneDrive.
  • GR-01 — Nothing is sent; the user reviews every draft before anything goes out.
  • SEC-01 — Single user: only the requesting PM uses and consumes the output; access is the user's own delegated data.
  • UX-01 — Primary user is a PM delegating a personal routine; output consumed as files for review.

Out of scope

  • FR-06 — Send the follow-up emails automatically. (Explicitly excluded)
  • DATA-03 — Use Teams chats or CRM records as additional sources. (Not evidenced)
  • FR-07 — Share drafts or the status note with others / multiple users. (Explicitly excluded)

Requirement Summary

10 in-scope requirements (FR-01..FR-05, DATA-01, DATA-02, GR-01, SEC-01, UX-01) and 3 out-of-scope rows (FR-06, FR-07, DATA-03). All IDs are derived from the chat request (no source IDs existed); out-of-scope rows do not drive gates, scores or complexity.

Assumptions

  • Week = Monday 00:00 to Friday run time in the user's time zone.
  • Customer = any meeting attendee or email participant outside the user's tenant domains (TBD rule).
  • Drafts are saved as editable documents in OneDrive; nothing is created in Outlook Drafts unless the user later asks.
  • Cowork scheduled personal routine availability is assumed but unconfirmed (verify in tenant).

Current State / Trigger Context

Today the PM manually reviews the week's calendar and inbox on Friday, writes follow-ups one by one and assembles a status note. Trigger: every Friday (FR-01).

Target Experience / Future State

On Friday the PM opens a dated OneDrive folder containing one follow-up draft per customer conversation and one weekly status note, each citing the meeting or email it came from. The PM edits and sends from Outlook; the assistant never sends (GR-01).

Security, Privacy, Compliance, and Governance

  • User-delegated access to own data only (SEC-01); no app-wide mailbox permissions.
  • No send permission — the assistant cannot email anyone (GR-01).
  • Drafts stay in the user's tenant OneDrive; customer content is not sent to external services.
  • Each plugin/tool (calendar, mail, OneDrive) is a security boundary: identity, scope and failure behaviour listed under Integrations.
  • Tenant controls, DLP and audit for Cowork: verify in tenant (gates TBD).

Primary journey sequence

  1. Schedule → Cowork assistant: Friday trigger fires (FR-01)
  2. Cowork assistant → Outlook calendar: List this week's meetings (DATA-01)
  3. Cowork assistant → Outlook mailbox: List this week's sent/received email (DATA-02)
  4. Cowork assistant → Customer rule: Filter to external customer conversations (FR-02)
  5. Cowork assistant → Follow-up skill: Draft one follow-up per conversation (FR-03)
  6. Cowork assistant → Status-note skill: Draft weekly status note (FR-04)
  7. Cowork assistant → OneDrive: Save drafts to the review folder (FR-05)
  8. Cowork assistant → PM: Notify: drafts ready for review (GR-01)
  9. PM → OneDrive: Review and edit drafts
  10. PM → Outlook mailbox: PM sends approved follow-ups manually (outside the assistant)

Solution Route Analysis

DA + skills

27/35 · Runner-up

Good grounding on the user's M365 mail and calendar and good governance, but it is a chat agent the PM must invoke each Friday and file save is an extra action.

Gate: TBD · Covers: DATA-01, DATA-02, FR-02, FR-03, FR-04, GR-01, SEC-01, UX-01
Cannot cover: FR-01 (declarative agent is user-initiated in chat; unattended Friday run not native); FR-05 (saving files needs an added bounded action — TBD)

Pro-code DA with MCP

17/35 · Over-engineered for current scope

Could cover all IDs, but needs owned code, hosting, Entra app registrations and MCP servers for a single-user, Stage 1-solvable routine (High complexity vs derived Medium).

Gate: TBD · Covers: FR-01, DATA-01, DATA-02, FR-02, FR-03, FR-04, FR-05, GR-01, SEC-01, UX-01
Cannot cover: —

Pro-code DA without MCP

16/35 · Over-engineered for current scope

Same pro-code ownership burden with direct Graph calls; no custom UI or protocol requirement justifies it.

Gate: TBD · Covers: FR-01, DATA-01, DATA-02, FR-02, FR-03, FR-04, FR-05, GR-01, SEC-01, UX-01
Cannot cover: —

Standard harness

23/35 · Not recommended

Not-fit signals match: the work is personal delegated drafting for one user ("only I", "my review"), not a predictable multi-user conversation. Flows could cover the schedule and file save, but the route adds environment/ALM overhead for one person.

Gate: TBD · Covers: FR-01, DATA-01, DATA-02, FR-02, FR-05, GR-01
Cannot cover: FR-03, FR-04 (heavy document drafting is a not-fit signal); SEC-01, UX-01 (built for shared/high-volume conversations, not one person's delegated work)

GHCP harness

25/35 · Over-engineered for current scope

Can do everything (document generation, skills, MCP), but plan-and-execute reasoning is not needed for a fixed weekly routine and Copilot Credits are consumed from build time for a one-person task.

Gate: TBD · Covers: FR-01, DATA-01, DATA-02, FR-02, FR-03, FR-04, FR-05, GR-01, SEC-01, UX-01
Cannot cover: —

Cowork plugins

31/35 · Primary

Native match to the dominant Delegated personal work components: the person who asks is the person who consumes the drafts (SEC-01, UX-01); reads own mail/meetings (DATA-01/02), drafts for review (FR-03/04, GR-01), saves to OneDrive (FR-05) and supports a personal Friday routine (FR-01). Tenant enablement is verify-in-tenant, so its gate is TBD, not Pass.

Gate: TBD · Covers: FR-01, DATA-01, DATA-02, FR-02, FR-03, FR-04, FR-05, GR-01, SEC-01, UX-01
Cannot cover: —

Scout

25/35 · Alternative (desktop)

Fits a single power user, but runs on one workstation, depends on local MCP access to M365 data, and has no shared governance plane. Viable as a prototype; MCP-ready design advised if chosen.

Gate: TBD · Covers: FR-01, FR-03, FR-04, GR-01, SEC-01, UX-01
Cannot cover: DATA-01, DATA-02, FR-05 (needs MCP/connector access to M365 mail, calendar and OneDrive from the workstation — TBD)

Ranking: Cowork plugins 31/35 > DA + skills 27/35 > Scout 25/35 > GHCP harness 25/35 > Standard harness 23/35 > Pro-code DA with MCP 17/35 > Pro-code DA without MCP 16/35 (Scout ahead of GHCP harness on tie-break toward lower complexity).

Key Technical Decisions

ProposedPrimary route: Cowork plugins — single-user delegated personal work (SEC-01, UX-01).
ProposedNo send capability: the assistant never holds a mail-send permission; the PM sends manually (GR-01).
ProposedCustomer selection is a deterministic domain rule, not an LLM judgment (FR-02) — separates reasoning from control.
ProposedStay at Stage 1: no Foundry or Agent Framework escalation (all in-scope IDs met).
